lines.note: Qetgiacu denotes settling or concluding a matter, matching the Portuguese determination. Votoxi, tçuquru supplies the Japanese verbal explanation; the headword's OCR space after Q is removed, while the printed comma between the Japanese forms is retained.

runs.text: ou aſſento ſobre algũa couſa que ſe conclue.

lines.note: This completes the definition as a resolution about something brought to a conclusion. The row is visibly indented like other continuations, correcting its unindented provisional placement; algũa keeps the nasal abbreviation.
Kuji wo ketgiaku suru illustrates determining a dispute or lawsuit. The paragraph mark introduces an example rather than a new headword; the Portuguese Aueriguar begins its translation.

runs.text: ou dar ſentença ſobre algũa demanda.

lines.note: The translation adds giving judgment on a legal dispute. This completes the example above; the long ſ in ſentença and ſobre and the abbreviated nasal in algũa remain as printed.

Qetgiǒ is explained through sadameru, to determine, and Idem refers back to the preceding decision sense. The final o has a visible caron; the compressed conjugational notation Sadame, uru is not expanded into a modern verb.

Qetjen is paraphrased by deciding and being so, then by a determination. Qeßuru is one word, correcting the draft’s internal space. The β-shaped double-s sort differs graphically from the adjacent upright types; its supplied italic classification is conservatively retained, with uncertainty about this single-sort font assignment, rather than making the entire word roman solely because it is Japanese. The β-shaped sort is not expanded into two separate long ſ characters.

Sadamaritaru koto means something that has been determined, supporting the Portuguese definition. The initial lowercase long ſ follows the alternative marker l, above; cou- continues as ſa on the next row.
This finishes couſa determinada, a determined thing or settled matter. Its inset position is a continuation indent, not the headword margin assigned by the OCR draft.

runs.text: O faltar, ou deixar de eſ-

lines.note: This Qetji concerns omitting a written character, paraphrased as ji wo kaku. The capital I followed by lowercase i is the dictionary's romanization of ji; eſ- starts the Portuguese eſcreuer across the physical break.

runs.text: creuer algũa letra de propoſito por a não ſaber,

lines.note: The writer deliberately leaves a character unwritten because it is not known. The visible t restores propoſito from OCR propoſio; the historical spelling and the separate a referring to letra are preserved.

runs.text: ou por outro reſpeito. ¶ Item, Lugar, ou

lines.note: The omission can also have another reason. A further sense starts after the paragraph mark, a place or space left blank; it is part of the same Qetji entry.

runs.text: eſpaço que ſe deixa em brãco nas cartas por re-

lines.note: This specifies a blank in a letter left out of reverence. Brãco uses the nasal abbreviation and re- begins reuerencia; neither the omitted nasal consonant nor the continuation is supplied on this physical row.
Uerencia completes the preceding re- as reverence, explaining the respectful blank. This short italic continuation is body text, not a usage label or page furniture.

runs.text: Qetji. Caquru coto. i, Coto caqe.

lines.note: The second Qetji is lack or deficiency rather than specifically a missing character. Caquru coto and Coto caqe give Japanese equivalents, and the Portuguese object of Falta de follows below.
This completes the definition as the lack of something. The tilde in algũa and long ſ in couſa are preserved without expansion or modernization.
Qetjo, explained by Coto caqi, likewise denotes want or shortage. The Portuguese mingua is left without a modern added accent; its object continues on the following row.

runs.text: algũa couſa. ¶ Item, Lugar em aberto que

lines.note: After completing the shortage sense, the entry adds an open or vacant place. The paragraph mark changes the sense within this entry rather than beginning a separate physical record.

runs.text: ſe deixa em algum liuro, eſcritura, &c.

lines.note: The vacant place is one left in a book or written document. Liuro and eſcritura retain their historical forms, and the final &c. closes the Qetjo explanation.

runs.text: Arte, ou doutrina que ſe eſcreue

lines.note: Qetmiacu introduces the written lineage of a teaching or art. The dictionary begins a long explanation of the document; its religious claims below are the historical authors' description, not independently verified assertions in this review.

runs.text: como ſerie predicamental, ou taboada dos pri-

lines.note: The document is compared to an ordered series or table of predecessors. Serie predicamental and taboada are retained as printed; pri- begins primeiros, continued on the next row.

runs.text: meiros que promulgarão aquella doutrina, ou

lines.note: This identifies the first promulgators of the doctrine or art. The printed promulgarão and aquella are not modernized, and ou links to arte below rather than ending the thought.

runs.text: arte com ſeus decendentes: & iſto dão os Bon-

lines.note: The table includes the founders' successors, and the account says that Buddhist clerics give this document to adherents. Decendentes lacks a written s after de in this copy and is preserved; Bon- continues into zos below.

runs.text: zos às vezes aſeus fregueſes, fazendolhes

lines.note: The clerics sometimes give the document to their adherents or parishioners. The grave accent in às and close aſeus setting are retained; fazendolhes introduces the authors' characterization of what the recipients are led to believe.

runs.text: creer que ſe ſaluarão, ou entrarão no numero

lines.note: The account says the recipients are led to believe they will be saved or included among certain eminent figures. The historical creer and future nasal endings are retained, and the set of people is specified below.

runs.text: da quelles homens inſignes, que eſtão eſcritos na-

lines.note: The eminent men are those listed in the document. The conspicuous separation da quelles is retained instead of being normalized to daquelles; the line-final na- starts naquelle below.

The list is described as written in red ink. The scan's catologo is retained as a printed irregularity, distinct from catalogo two rows later; Qet- begins the roman Japanese example, with its hyphen in the same typeface rather than italic.

Qetmiacu wo tsutayuru means transmitting the teaching or lineage document. The final ru is abraded and separated in the setting; the chosen tçutayu ru preserves the supplied spacing rather than silently repairing it. The Portuguese starts teaching and handing over the catalogue.

Gar completes entregar, handing over this catalogue. A second Japanese example begins receiving the lineage; its verb is divided as ſaz-zucaru over the row boundary, retaining the printed doubled z across that division.

runs.text: Receber do Bonzo este eſcrito jun-

lines.note: Zucaru completes the verb of receiving. The translation describes receiving this writing from a Buddhist cleric, and jun- starts juntamente; Bonzo is the Portuguese designation used by the source.

runs.text: tamente com o nome do Bonzo parecendolhe

lines.note: The document is received together with the cleric's name. The attached pronoun in parecendolhe is left as printed, leading to the recipient's belief stated on the next row.

runs.text: que por alli ſe ha de ſaluar.

lines.note: This completes the source's account of a belief that salvation will come by that means. The scan clearly supplies alli, correcting OCR lli; the sentence is reported as part of the dictionary's explanation, not adopted as the reviewer's claim.
Qetnicu denotes blood and flesh, explicitly paired with Chi and xiximura. Car- is the beginning of Portuguese carne and is completed on the next physical row.
Ne completes carne, flesh. The following S is an upright written-usage label, separate from the italic Portuguese definition.

Qetrui means tears of blood, as Chi no namida makes explicit. The visible t restores the headword from OCR Qerui; the supplied NINJAL lexical index independently corroborates Qetrui, but the scan controls its spelling (Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, v202510; NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima, Taichi Aida; CC BY 4.0; https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html).
Gue completes ſangue in the tears-of-blood gloss. The upright S marks written usage and is not part of the italic word ending.

Qetyen and qechiyen are alternative forms for establishing a connection, with Yenuo muſubu as the Japanese explanation. The italic Vide begins a reference to the earlier entry rather than a further Japanese synonym.

This completes Vide ſuprà Qechiyen, directing the reader to the earlier article. The word Qechiyen is fully roman and contiguous; the OCR's internal space after Q is removed, while the grave accent in ſuprà is retained.
Qetyeqi is explained by blood and fluid, Chi and xiru. The Portuguese pairs sangue with humor in its historical bodily-fluid sense; the description of that fluid continues below.

runs.text: pingue que eſta na ſuperficie da carne em ho-

lines.note: The fluid is described as fatty or rich and present at the surface of flesh. Pingue and unaccented eſta are retained; ho- begins homens on the following row.
This completes the description as applying to fat and plump people. Nedeos is the historical printed adjective and is not replaced with its modern accented form.
Qetza denotes an empty seat or place, with Cacuru za as the Japanese paraphrase. The source's Cacuru is retained, and va- begins vazio in the Portuguese gloss.

runs.text: zio, ou onde falta alguem que ſe cuſtuma alli

lines.note: After completing vazio, the explanation specifies a place whose customary occupant is absent. The historical forms alguem, cuſtuma and alli remain unchanged, and the infinitive completing the description is below.
Aſſentar completes the phrase about someone who usually sits there. Both long ſ characters are retained; this is an indented continuation, not a separate headword.

Qev means rare, and Qevno gui nari gives the example 'it is a rare matter'. The headword's full stop remains roman with the headword rather than opening the italic gloss as in the provisional markup; the historical final v is retained.
The Portuguese translates the preceding example as a rare thing. S is an upright written-usage marker and is separated from the italic translation.
Qeuai and its principal parts describe adorning the face with cosmetics. The scan reads roſto, correcting OCR roſta; both displayed long-vowel marks in ǒ and ǒta are carons, not circumflexes.

Kao wo kewau illustrates applying cosmetics to the face. The contracted form qeuǒ retains its caron, and the row is complete above the bottom rule; the related noun begins at the top of the right column.

runs.text: Affeite, ou poſturas que poem as mo-

lines.note: The noun Qeuai denotes facial adornment or cosmetics applied by women. The scan separates poem as and starts the historical molheres as mo-, not the draft's joined poemas ma-; the word continues at the start of the next row.

Lheres completes molheres, followed by the example Qeuaiuo ſuru, applying makeup. The scan restores the continuation from OCR malheres and prints Con- entirely in italic. The inset first word requires a continuation indent absent from the draft.

runs.text: certar, & affeitar o roſto com poſturas.

lines.note: Certar completes Concertar, followed by adorning the face with cosmetics. The translation remains wholly italic, and the historical affeitar and poſturas are not replaced by modern vocabulary.
Qeuaxij describes steepness or roughness, initially of terrain. The Japanese double-vowel ending ij is retained, and the Portuguese ingreme is left without a modern added accent.
Mountains and roads supply the literal examples, followed by Qeuaxij mi-, continued as michi below. The whole adjective is roman and contiguous; the draft's internal Q euaxij space is removed.

Chi completes michi, and yama supplies the mountain example. The Portuguese translation describes a road or mountain range and divides aſpera after aſ-; the Japanese words and their &c. remain in the roman span.

Pera completes aſpera, with fragoſa adding ruggedness. Permet. introduces the metaphorical extension to a person; its close setting is preserved rather than expanded to Per met. on analogy with other pages.
Qeuaxij fito describes a difficult person of bad disposition. The scan supplies the narrow i in ruim, correcting OCR rum; con- starts condição below.
This completes condição, the person's character or disposition. The short continuation closes the figurative Qeuaxij sense and is not related to the plant entry below.
This Qexi is the plant name, glossed as dormideiras, poppies. It is distinct from the homonymous verbs immediately below; no modern species-level identification is inserted into the transcription.

Qexi, with principal parts ſu and eita, means extinguishing or erasing. Fiuo qeſu is extinguishing a fire; the supplied historical eita form remains unchanged rather than being replaced by a modern paradigm.

The first translation is extinguishing the fire, followed by erasing written characters. The second example is Iiuo qeſu, with capital I plus lowercase i for ji; the line starts near the outer text margin in the scan, so its original unindented placement is retained.
Tra completes letra. The next idiom, kimo wo kesu, expresses being stunned or terrified; the Portuguese renders it as being astonished or becoming something specified on the next row.
Attonito finishes the astonishment example. Doku wo kesu then means counteracting poison; the printed line ends a- even though a functions as the Portuguese article before peçonha on the next row.

runs.text: peçonha com mezinha, ou contra peçonha.

lines.note: The translation describes counteracting poison with a remedy or antidote. Mezinha and the two-word contra peçonha remain in the source's historical form; this is a lexical example, not medical advice.

This separate application of Qexi concerns gilding or silvering, with Facu and Dei as the objects in the example. The roman alternative marker l, and both printed Japanese expressions are preserved; the metal-coating explanation follows below.

runs.text: Dourar, ou pratear cõ prata, ouro, ou latão

lines.note: The Portuguese explains gilding or silvering with silver, gold, or brass. The nasal abbreviation cõ is retained, and the physical line break comes before the preparation of those metals is described.
This specifies that the material is made into a slurry or paste. The short italic continuation completes the gilding sense and does not introduce another Japanese expression.

runs.text: Modo de dourar desta maneira. No

lines.note: Here Qexi is the noun for this manner of gilding. The explanation leads into a regional alternative, with No at the end of this row governing Cami on the next.

The source says that the upper-region term is Qeximecqi. Cami is embedded in the italic Portuguese frame, while the cited word Qeximecqi is roman; the OCR's internal space after Q is removed without modernizing the spelling.
This Qexi verb is glossed as saving and, in another sense, assuming a different form. The principal part ſuru is distinct from the earlier erasing verb's ſu; To- starts Tomar across the row boundary.
Mar completes Tomar outra figura, taking another form. This explains the transformation sense without silently replacing the preceding Saluar with a different religious term.
Qexicaqe describes setting an animal on someone or provoking it. The Portuguese Aſſular is retained in its historical spelling, with the animals and intended action specified below.

runs.text: caẽs, ou outras feras pera que mordão, &c.

lines.note: Dogs or other fierce animals are incited to bite. The scan places the tilde on e in caẽs; pera and mordão are preserved rather than normalized to modern Portuguese.

The source gives Foximecaxi, ſu as the lower-region alternative for inciting the animals. Ximo is a Japanese regional name within the italic Portuguese sentence; the cited verb is roman, and Am- starts Ambos below.

runs.text: bos eſtes verbos ordinariamenteſe vſão em ma-

lines.note: Ambos completes the statement about both verbs, which are ordinarily used in the matter specified below. The scan reads vſão, 'are used', not OCR vão, and separates em ma-; the close ordinariamenteſe setting is retained.
This completes materia de caẽs: the verbs are normally used of dogs. The tilde remains on e in caẽs, matching the earlier occurrence in this entry.

Qexicaranu is here explained as an intensive, Fanafadaxiqu, very or exceedingly. The scan restores Muito from OCR Mito; the source's broad use is qualified on the next row rather than restricted to the modern disapproving sense.
The intensive can apply in a good or bad sense. Qexicaranu tei supplies the example of an extraordinary manner; the grave accent in mà is retained.
The first example is translated as an extraordinary manner or appearance. The printed extra ordinaria separation is retained, and Qe- begins a second Japanese example on the next row.

Qexicaranu tenqi gives the unfavorable application, very bad weather. The Portuguese is closely set as Muitoruim in the supplied reading; it is retained rather than regularized merely because the modern phrase has a space.

Qexin concerns a transformed body or manifestation, with Qeſuru mi as the Japanese explanation. Qeſuru is one contiguous roman word, correcting the OCR split after Q; the nasal abbreviation trãs- begins the Portuguese transfiguration description.
This completes transfigurada and says that the body or substance has been changed into another. Noutra remains the source's contracted form, and the short row closes the entry.
Qexiqi denotes appearance or countenance here, glossed as Sembrante. The OCR's internal Q exiqi space is removed; Tçuuamonodo- begins the quoted example about warriors and continues below.

runs.text: mo firumu qexiqini miyetari qeru. Taif.

lines.note: Tçuuamonodomo completes 'warriors', who appeared to show signs of shrinking back. Enlargement shows a damaged final stroke of the initial m, supporting retained mo rather than a superficially plausible no. Taif. is the upright citation label for the Taiheiki, with the book reference below.

runs.text: Lib. 32. Os ſoldados dauão moſtras de me-

lines.note: The citation is to book 32, followed by the Portuguese translation: the soldiers showed signs of fear. Me- begins medo, which is completed on the next physical row.

After completing medo, the example Qexiqiga cauaru describes a change of countenance. Enlargement shows nasal marks over both e and a in ſẽbrãte, restoring the first tilde omitted by OCR; no terminal full stop is supplied where none is visible before the rule.

This Qexǒ is makeup or facial adornment. The caron is retained, and the example begins Qe-; the provisional short-s representations in the st sequences of rosto and posturas are not subjected to a systematic ligature reclassification.
Qexǒ ſuru completes the makeup example, applying cosmetics to the face. This row retains its existing long-ſ representations rather than being forced to match the adjacent row's st encoding.

The second Qexǒ concerns a transformed being, with fengue as the alternative expression. The scan has a line-final hyphen after fengue, not the OCR period; no mono on the next row continues that Japanese expression.

Fengue-no mono completes the alternative, followed by a transformed thing or one that has taken another form. The scan reads tomou, correcting OCR tomos; q̃ is the printed abbreviation for que and is not expanded.
This finishes the definition as taking another form. The italic continuation belongs to the transformation entry, not the following compound about battle.

Qexǒicuſa is explained as a light or brief engagement rather than a fully committed battle. Enlargement reads peleja, with one j and no preceding separate i, correcting the draft's peleija; the Japanese long ſ is retained.
The fighting is described as brief and not undertaken in earnest. Breuemente and propoſito retain the historical spelling and unaccented form rather than modern Portuguese normalization.
Qexxi means deciding or settling an outcome. The scan distinctly shows two long ſ characters in ſſuru, restoring the one omitted by OCR; So- begins the quotation's sono on the next row.

runs.text: no fiua faya curegatani nareba, xôbuua

lines.note: Sono hi wa haya kuregata ni nareba says that the day was already drawing toward evening. Xôbuua is the topic, the contest or its outcome, continued below; the circumflex in xôbuua and the historical faya are preserved.

The quotation concludes that the contest will not be decided. Enlargement resolves the ending as majij, with j-i-j rather than OCR maju; the dictionary's ij convention gives the extended final vowel, not an invented u. Upright Feiq. supplies the Heike citation, followed by book 4 and the Portuguese Sendo ja, correcting Scobo. The translation continues beyond the page; the catchword tar- is separate furniture.
